current_status.from: Rescinded by court order as of 2026-09-23. Imperial County Superior Court Judge Jeffrey B. Jones entered judgment 2026-09-04 in favor of developer Imperial Valley Computer Manufacturing, LLC, finding neither Ordinance 1616 (the original moratorium) nor Ordinance 1618 (its ~10-month-15-day extension) made the causal finding of a 'current and immediate threat to public health, safety, or welfare' required by Gov. Code section 65858. A peremptory writ of mandate issued 2026-09-11 directs the County and Board of Supervisors to set aside both ordinances and stop using them to withhold, suspend, or refuse data-center permits. The County has said (per KYMA, 2026-09-22) it is working on a new moratorium addressing the court's concerns; no replacement had been adopted as of 2026-09-23. The Data Center Advisory Committee, created alongside the moratorium, continues to meet (inaugural meeting 2026-09-17) and is unaffected by the ruling. Separately, a different judge (L. Brooks Anderholt) has ordered a full CEQA environmental review of the underlying data center project in a related case, so the project itself remains stalled notwithstanding the moratorium's invalidation.
current_status.to: Ordinances 1616 and 1618 were repealed and set aside by the Board on October 6, 2026 in compliance with the court writ; the county said the urgency repeal took effect immediately. A separate October 6 moratorium was reported in local news; its later status was not verified.
current_status.reason: Official county announcement identifies actual repeal; separate reported action must not be conflated with original.

outcome.from: Moratorium (Ordinances 1616 and 1618) adopted and extended to run through mid-2027, then invalidated by the Imperial County Superior Court (Judge Jeffrey B. Jones) in Imperial Valley Computer Manufacturing, LLC v. County of Imperial: judgment entered 2026-09-04, peremptory writ of mandate issued 2026-09-11 ordering the County to set aside and cease enforcing both ordinances because their findings did not satisfy Gov. Code section 65858's 'current and immediate threat' standard. The County has 30 days after service of the writ to file a return; county officials say they are preparing a new moratorium that addresses the court's findings. The Data Center Advisory Committee process continues separately.
outcome.to: The Board repealed and set aside Ordinances 1616 and 1618 on October 6, 2026, in compliance with the Superior Court writ. A separate 45-day moratorium was reported adopted that day; its later status is unresolved.
outcome.reason: Update the original ordinance history without assigning it the new action.

current_status.from: Active; permanent citywide data center prohibition in place. Measure NDC passed at the June 2, 2026 special election (10,388 Yes / 1,372 No, per the LA County Registrar-Recorder's certified canvass); results certified by the City Clerk on June 30, 2026 and declared by City Council Resolution No. 2026-R56 on July 1, 2026 (unanimous, 5-0). Companion Ordinance No. 2280 (General Plan amendment prohibiting all data centers citywide) was adopted by Council on July 2, 2026, effective on or about July 11, 2026 (10 days after election-result certification, per Elections Code section 9217).
current_status.to: The City adopted urgency Ordinance 2276 on April 20, 2026 establishing a citywide data center prohibition effective immediately upon adoption, and adopted Ordinance 2279 on May 6, 2026 to implement Measure NDC, with its effective date tied to the measure. The election result, certification, and precise termination of the temporary moratorium require independent verification.
current_status.reason: The signed ordinances replace unsupported references to Ordinance 2280 and a July 2 adoption.

outcome.from: Moratorium extended through 2027-01-21 (superseded in practice by permanent action); permanent citywide prohibition codified by ordinance on 2026-04-20; voters ratified the prohibition via Measure NDC on 2026-06-02 (10,388 Yes / 1,372 No), with results certified July 1, 2026 and companion Ordinance No. 2280 adopted July 2, 2026.
outcome.to: The City adopted urgency Ordinance 2276 on April 20, 2026 and Ordinance 2279 on May 6, 2026. The latter ties its effective date to Measure NDC; election result and legal relationship to the temporary ordinance require verification.
